cost.a: It depends on three things: the size of the space, the state of the shell, and how much is made rather than bought. We’ll tell you on the first call whether your number is realistic, including when it isn’t. After the site visit you get a range; after detail design, a fixed price on one contract. Kitchen equipment, deposits and licence fees sit outside that number, and we’ll help you plan for them.

time.a: A 100–150 m² café usually takes 10–14 weeks from signed design to opening: 4–6 weeks of drawings and approvals, then 6–8 weeks on site. Restaurants and bars with full kitchens and extraction take 16–24 weeks. The build is rarely the critical path. Approvals and long-lead items are: kitchen equipment, custom lighting, stone. We order those early.

licences.q: Do you handle licences and permits?
licences.a: We draw what your landlord and the authorities need — fire and exit layouts, extraction routes, signage permissions, mall fit-out submissions — and design to those conditions from day one, so nothing is ripped out later. The licences themselves (in India: food, trade, excise, fire NOC) are held in your name. We work alongside your licensing consultant, or introduce one we trust.

open.q: Can you work while we’re open?
open.a: Yes. Most refreshes happen that way. We phase the works around trading: nights, your quiet day, or a short planned closure for the noisy parts. Joinery is made off-site, so time on site is days rather than weeks. We agree dust, noise and access rules with you before anyone picks up a drill.

contractors.a: We do. On a design & build project every trade works for us, under one contract and one programme, with one of our site leads in charge. You get a weekly site walk and a daily diary. You don’t get calls from the electrician.

designer.q: I already have a designer. Can you still help?
designer.a: Yes. We build other designers’ drawings, and we’re good at it because we draw too. We review the package, flag anything that will cost you on site, price it properly and keep your designer in the loop on every change. The design stays theirs.

kitchen.a: We plan the kitchen with your chef and a specialist kitchen consultant: the layout, the pass, the services and the extraction. We build the room around it and coordinate the equipment supplier. We don’t sell equipment, so we have no reason to over-specify it.

small.a: Probably not. A counter, a lighting fix or one wall of joinery can change how a room trades. They’re on the menu as small plates, and they get the same senior team as a flagship.

see.q: Will I know what it looks like before it’s built?
see.a: Yes. You walk through it in 3D, handle every finish on a sample board, and for the pieces that matter most — the counter, a banquette, the bar top — we build a full-size section before we make the rest.

city.q: Will you work in my city?
city.a: Very likely. We work across India, and abroad with our own site lead and a local contractor under our contract. Recent projects include Lisbon and Dubai.

sectors.label: Cafés
sectors.headline: Cafés that earn their living *before ten*.
sectors.intro: A café is judged at 08:15, with the queue at the door. We plan the counter first — order, make, pick-up, bin — so two baristas can do the work of three. Then the room: seats for laptops and for prams, daylight on the pastry case, power where people actually sit, and a corner table someone will claim every morning.

seo.title: Café design & build — Two Squares
seo.description: Cafés, bakeries and espresso bars designed and built by Two Squares: counters planned for the morning rush, rooms that hold the afternoon.

points.title: The counter comes first
points.text: Order, make, pick-up, bin, in that order along one run. Two baristas do the work of three, and the queue never crosses the pick-up.

points.title: Daylight on the pastry case
points.text: The case goes where the morning light lands, and warm lamps take over after lunch. Pastry sells on how it looks.

points.title: Power where people sit
points.text: Sockets at the bench and along the window ledge, where laptops actually land. Nobody runs a cable across the aisle.

points.title: A corner table
points.text: Every good café has one seat someone claims every morning. We draw it early, and we light it last.

menu.headline: A counter, a refresh or the *whole café*.
menu.lede: Straight from the menu. Order one and the form arrives with your café already filled in.

sectors.label: Restaurants
sectors.headline: Dining rooms with a *pulse*.
sectors.intro: We walk the service before we choose a finish: host to table, table to pass, pass to wash-up. Every metre a server saves is a metre of calm in the room. Then we make it warm: acoustics you can talk over at full covers, banquettes worth waiting for, and light that flatters the food and the faces.

seo.title: Restaurant design & build — Two Squares
seo.description: Restaurants designed and built by Two Squares: plans drawn around the service, acoustics for full covers and light that flatters food and faces.

points.title: The service path
points.text: Host to table, table to pass, pass to wash-up. We walk it before we choose a finish: every metre a server saves is a metre of calm in the room.

points.title: Acoustics at full covers
points.text: Absorption in the ceiling, the banquette backs and under the tables. We test it with the room full, so a table for two can still talk at nine.

points.title: Banquettes worth waiting for
points.text: Made in our workshop, with a seat you can stay in for three courses. They seat more covers than loose chairs, and they’re the seats people ask for.

points.title: Light for food and faces
points.text: Warm and low over the tables, brighter at the pass, and set on scenes that dim through the evening without anyone touching a switch.

menu.headline: A test-fit, new light or the *whole room*.
menu.lede: Straight from the menu. Order one and the form arrives with your restaurant already filled in.

sectors.label: Bars
sectors.headline: Rooms built for *late*.
sectors.intro: Everything in a bar faces one way. We design the back-bar as the stage and the room as the audience, draw the stations with your head bartender, and put the lighting on scenes so the room changes without anyone touching a switch. Finishes are chosen for citrus, sugar and 2am.

seo.title: Bar design & build — Two Squares
seo.description: Cocktail bars and late rooms designed and built by Two Squares: back-bars lit as the stage, stations drawn with your bartenders, finishes that last.

points.title: The back-bar is the stage
points.text: The bottles are lit as the set and the room is kept darker, so every eye goes to where the drinks are made.

points.title: A speed rail at every station
points.text: Drawn with your head bartender: well, rail, ice, glass wash and garnish, all within reach. Two bartenders can hold 1am.

points.title: Lighting on scenes
points.text: Early, service and late, on a timer. The room changes through the night and nobody reaches for a switch mid-shift.

points.title: Finishes for citrus, sugar and 2am
points.text: Bar tops sealed against acid, brass that takes a polish and upholstery that wipes down at close.

sectors.label: Shops
sectors.headline: Retail you walk *slower* in.
sectors.intro: A shopfront gets about three seconds with someone walking past at 4 km/h. We design for those three seconds, then for the walk to the back wall, then for the till. Fixtures that disappear, light that renders colour truthfully, and kits of parts that travel to the next city.
